## Actual numerical result: a useful new failure

The full new numerical matrix ran to an actual failure in **67.37 s**:

| Pair | Result |
| --- | --- |
| H: D1 versus P1 | FMFT and candidate RustRed agree, including within-backend identity |
| H: D7 versus P7 | pass |
| H: D1 D2 versus P1 P2 | pass |
| H: D5 D6 versus P5 P6 | pass; 12,554 new candidate recurrence applications |
| FG: D1 versus P1 | pass |
| FG: D7 versus P7 | **fails within FMFT itself** before the RustRed pair check |
| Remaining ten pairs | not reached |

The failure is the real coefficient of epsilon^-4: **1.5 versus 0**, with the
test reporting relative error 2. No tolerance was changed. This does **not**
yet identify whether the problem lies in the fixture, shared routing/FeynKit
preprocessing, or FMFT's scalar adapter. It is not evidence of a RustRed-rule
failure, since the assertion occurs first in the FMFT lane. Keep both inputs
and inspect their canonical and tensor-reduced forms before modifying code.

   Omit the custom family names from example generation inputs to match the

3. Integrate these into the opt-in public RustRed method without changing its

4. Rerun both suites through the public method with an invalid FORM path,
   plus relevant lower-loop/default regressions. Then commit/push and stop as
